Commentary.Commentary: It's been a thrilling conclusion to the warm-up games. Now, the excitement shifts to the ICC Women's World Cup, which kicks off on September 30, 2025, with India Women facing Sri Lanka Women. We are also covering the Asia Cup 2025 Final, where arch-rivals India and Pakistan are facing off. Pakistan, batting first, have been bundled out for 146 and all India needs is 147 to lift the Asia Cup. All you need to do is switch tabs for action from that contest. Stay tuned for updates from these high-stakes tournaments! Cheers for now.

Earlier, Pakistan Women posted 229 runs on the board, thanks to a strong partnership between Sidra Amin and Sidra Nawaz (57 runs) and a crucial 65-run partnership between captain Fatima Sana and Aliya Riaz. Sana showed remarkable resilience, scoring 64 runs before being dismissed. The Proteas' bowlers, Ayabonga Khaka and Masabata Klaas, took two wickets each, while Nadine De Klerk, Tumi Sekhukhune, Chloe Tryon, and Annerie Dercksen secured one wicket each.

Pakistan's bowling showed flashes of brilliance, particularly from Diana Baig, who bowled exceptionally well and took a couple of crucial wickets. Although the rest of the bowling unit didn't quite complement her efforts as she'd have liked, other bowlers like Fatima Sana, Omaima Sohail, Syeda Aroob Shah, and Sadia Iqbal chipped in with one wicket each.

South Africa Women faced a tough start in their chase, losing early wickets. However, Sune Luus and Anneke Bosch steadied the ship with a crucial partnership, both scoring half-centuries. After retiring to give others a chance to bat, Chloe Tryon and Nadine de Klerk contributed well with the bat and wrapped up the win for South Africa, securing a 4-wicket victory. Chloe Tryon went on to score the winning runs.

South Africa Women have emerged victorious in this warm-up match, defeating Pakistan Women by 4 wickets. This win will boost the Proteas' confidence as they head into the main event, carrying positive momentum into the tournament.
